item.title: Pectoral / Anterior Shoulder MFR
clinicalUse: Anterior chest/pectoral tightness limiting comfortable shoulder elevation
Postural/overhead movement restriction as an adjunct
patientPosition: Supine with arm supported in comfortable abduction.
contact: Broad contact over pectoral tissue lateral to sternum and near anterior shoulder, avoiding breast tissue and neurovascular bundle.
forceDirection: Slow cross-hand or longitudinal fascial load away from restriction, within comfort.
mistakes: Assuming 'tightness' is the only cause of shoulder pain.
safety: Respect post-mastectomy/oncology precautions, wound healing and lymphedema risk.
item.visualCue: Broad pectoral contact → Slow fascial load → Re-test elevation/ER.

subTechniques.name: Pectoral Fascial Release
subTechniques.target: Pectoralis major/minor and anterior shoulder fascia
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve selected anterior chest/shoulder soft-tissue mobility before active scapular and shoulder work.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the arm supported in a comfortable amount of abduction.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the pectoral fascia, staying away from breast tissue, axillary neurovascular structures and sensitive surgical regions.
subTechniques.direction: Sustain a gentle diagonal or lateral tissue load toward the restriction; do not force end-range shoulder stretch.
subTechniques.dosage: 60–120 seconds per contact with immediate reassessment.
subTechniques.reassess: Shoulder elevation, scapular posterior tilt/retraction and reach.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The goal is not to 'break adhesions'; use the technique to change movement tolerance and then reinforce with active exercise.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Shoulder / Latissimus Fascial Release
subTechniques.target: Posterior cuff, latissimus and posterior axillary fascia
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve selected overhead/elevation tolerance where posterior/lateral soft-tissue restriction is relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Side-lying or supine with the arm supported in a comfortable elevated position.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the posterior-lateral shoulder and latissimus region.
subTechniques.direction: Apply slow sustained tissue loading along the restricted fascial direction while keeping the rib cage controlled.
subTechniques.reassess: Shoulder flexion, internal rotation and overhead reach.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Control rib flare so a change in trunk position is not mistaken for a shoulder mobility gain.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid aggressive pressure in acute rotator-cuff injury.
